column3: MT 1:18. “Said to build” is rendered “decided to build,” and “a house for his royalty” as “a royal palace for himself.”
MT 2:2. NASB supplies “word” and “so do for me”; the Hebrew sentence is left incomplete.
MT 2:3. “Make smoke” is rendered “burn,” and “the row of continuity” as “the showbread continually.” “This is on Israel” is rendered “this being required … in Israel.”
MT 2:5. “Retain strength” is rendered “is able,” and “heavens of the heavens” as “highest heavens.”
MT 2:6. “Bronze” is rendered “brass”; NASB supplies “fabrics” and “to work.” “Appointed” is rendered “provided.”
MT 2:7. “Fir” is rendered “cypress.” “There!” is rendered “indeed,” and NASB supplies “will work.”
MT 2:8. “And act wonderfully” is rendered “and wonderful.”
MT 2:9. “Wounds” is rendered “crushed”; the Hebrew word is odd here, and the meaning is uncertain.
MT 2:10. “In a document” is rendered “in a letter”; NASB supplies quotation marks for a short message.
MT 2:11. “Insight” is rendered “discretion,” and “a house for his royalty” as “a royal palace for himself.”
MT 2:12. NASB writes “Huram-abi” as one name; the meaning of the second part is uncertain.
MT 2:13. “A son of a woman of the daughters of Dan” is rendered “the son of a Danite woman.” NASB supplies “fabrics” and “to work,” and renders “design any design” as “execute any design.”
MT 2:14. Word order is changed; NASB supplies “Now then.”
MT 2:15. “According to all your need” is rendered “whatever timber you need.”
MT 2:17. “To compel to labor” is rendered “to make … work.”
